runConfig.positivePrompt: Scientific educational image-to-video for ages five to fourteen. Static locked wide camera, one continuous forward-only five-second shot with no cuts. Preserve the attached approved still as the exact first-frame Iguanodon bernissartensis identity, robust quadrupedal anatomy, left-facing full-body composition, lighting, palette, skin markings, woodland, ground, and crop reference. Exactly one complete Iguanodon remains with one beaked skull, a deep torso, two forelimbs with the original conical thumb spikes and weight-bearing central digits, exactly two hind limbs, four planted feet total, and one complete long tail. After a brief opening hold, the dinosaur itself raises the complete skull, connected neck, throat, shoulder base, and upper chest together by a clear five to seven degrees in one smooth continuous direction. The closed beak, jaw proportions, eye, cheek, thumb spikes, hand shape, and neck thickness remain constant. The final second holds the higher alert pose. Keep the pelvis, all four planted feet, every readable digit, both hands, both thumb spikes, and the full tail at their source coordinates. Keep all trees, plants, shadows, and sky completely still. No return, reverse, second nod, chewing, step, body turn, or loop.
